In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SMPSs approach to task-parallelism can be a good choice when the target architecture is a multicore cluster, and the legacy code is a message-passing implementation of an algorithm that does not have a task-parallel variant.
the SMPSs approach is able to achieve a better performance in the Cholesky routine, and that it is also more scalable than the original Sca-LAPACK routine and the two other recent implementations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the viability of SMPSs for the parallelization of legacy dense linear algebra codes.
we are able to obtain a performance comparable to the state of the art, while avoiding a complete rewrite of the original Sca-LAPACK code.

SMPSs provides an interesting alternative to MPI for the parallelization of message-passing dense linear algebra routines, which is especially attractive in cases where a large amount of task-parallelism is present.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SMPSs model provides a powerful abstraction for programming dense matrix computations in a message-passing environment, and that the programming effort required for adapting a legacy code to this model is limited.
the SMPSs model can be used to parallelize the Cholesky algorithm in ScaL APACK with little modications to the original sequential code, and with a limited programming overhead.
the use of task-parallelism can improve the performance of dense linear algebra routines in clusters of multicore machines, even when the code is based on a message-passing model.
